sequence.edge_key: scrub(cleaning equipment and material)|||insert(cleaning equipment and material)

per_session.semi_markov: jump chain + bridge holding time (gap_s_*) per edge
per_session.note: P(next spine | current spine) is recomputed over the spine state space. It is NOT the micro P(next action | current action) and the two must never be shown on the same edge. Lumping a Markov chain is not guaranteed to preserve the Markov property (Kemeny & Snell), so this is a first-order approximation of the induced process, not an exact rewrite of the original chain.

faithfulness.rule: A macro edge is legal iff the two spine actions were consecutive in the spine, with every action between them recorded on the edge. An edge with an empty bridge is a direct transition and must also occur in the raw adjacency set. Bridged edges are NOT expected in the raw adjacency set — testing them with the micro fabrication rule would flag every one of them by design.

canonical_spine_report.note: Every action in canonical_spine was performed by every session, in this order. Nodes marked tier='connector' were NOT part of that common sequence; they are the shortest observed route joining two spine actions that were never directly adjacent. Every edge on the path was observed — none is fabricated.

filter_report.rule: window: an action is kept if its window overlaps an annotated step_times window. span: an action is kept if it falls inside the task span, min(first prep, first step) to max(last step). Excluded actions are removed from the motion graph only; they remain in the sequence, the swimlane and graph_unfiltered.
